en: Uppannattikādi, Kusalattika (The Triplet of the Wholesome)

A non-arisen unwholesome state is a condition, by way of object-condition (*ārammaṇapaccaya*), for an arisen wholesome state. [There are] seven [types] in the case of the object, six in the case of the predominance (*adhipati*), and seven in the case of the decisive support (*upanissaya*).

A non-arisen unwholesome state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an arisen unwholesome state. [There are] six [types] in the case of the object, six in the case of the predominance, and six in the case of the decisive support.
A non-non-arisen indeterminate state is a condition, by way of root-condition (*hetupaccaya*), for an arisen indeterminate state. ... [Three types].
A non-arisen indeterminate state is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an arisen indeterminate state. (Abbreviated. Under root: three;
under object: seven; under predominance: four; under conascence and dependence: three; under decisive support: seven ... pe ...
under non-disappearance: three. The past triad is similar to the arisen triad.
